title: Chapter 188: One Is Enough
html:
The hall was packed, with more visitors waiting downstairs and elevators delivering a constant stream of newcomers. At 10:00 a.m., Tian Teng Medical School’s proprietor finally appeared. He was of average height, with closely cropped hair, and looked to be in his thirties.

Two models in revealing nurse costumes followed him. Their makeup was deathly white, but their flirtatious gazes remained lively. The man tested the loudspeaker, took his place on the steps before the entrance, and began, “Everyone, thank you for your generous support. Tian Teng Medical School has always maintained…”

Chen Ge looked over the two models and ignored the introductory speech. He was already considering a cute but alluring costume for Xu Wan at the Haunted House’s next special event.

The man talked for two to three minutes before finally getting to the point.

“Our team updates and optimizes the Haunted House every six months. With help from foreign professionals, we continually renew every scare. As proprietor, it is my duty to tell you that Tian Teng Medical School is more terrifying than any other Haunted House on the market!

“We pursue the most authentic horror, unlike certain unscrupulous attractions that hire paid trolls to inflate their online popularity. They think they’re clever, and some people do fall for those tricks, but frankly, I find such behavior laughable.”

Growing impatient with the slander, Chen Ge pushed through the crowd. After considerable effort, he reached the ticket counter. “One ticket, please.”

“Did you book a ticket online?”

“No.”

“I’m sorry, today’s tickets are sold out. You can wait until this afternoon in case a spot opens.”

“The tickets are all gone?”

Onstage, the proprietor continued. “If ordinary Haunted Houses are first-generation attractions, Tian Teng Medical School is fourth generation, integrating a wide range of advanced technology!

“Today marks our first day in Jiujiang. To demonstrate the experience, I will randomly choose four visitors and equip them with audio recorders and portable heart monitors. Their microphones will play through our speakers, while their heart rates appear live onscreen. You’ll witness exactly how frightening our Haunted House is!”

The crowd erupted in cheers before he had even finished. Whether the enthusiasm was genuine or staged was impossible to tell.

“Each ticket has a code, and a random-number generator will select our lucky guests.” The man nodded toward the sales counter, and the staff began the drawing.

Chen Ge had heard enough. The man was elevating his own attraction by trampling on Chen Ge’s, and he would not accept it quietly.

“Wait!” Raising one hand, Chen Ge stepped onto the stage. “You claimed your attraction is frightening while others rely on paid trolls to manufacture popularity. I disagree.”

The man frowned. If not for the crowd, he would have called for security to haul Chen Ge out.

“I own Western Jiujiang’s House of Horrors—the attraction you’ve been happily slandering online. Two nights ago, my livestream drew more than 600,000 viewers.”

When Chen Ge walked to the stage, there was a familiar voice from the crowd that called out. “Boss?!”

Chen Ge followed the voice and saw He San and Gao Ru Xue standing in the crowd.

“Why are you here?” Chen Ge was baffled to find He San openly supporting a competitor. “If you wanted to visit a Haunted House, why didn’t you come to mine?”

He San had no idea how to answer. In front of Tian Teng Medical School’s proprietor, he could hardly admit that Boss Chen’s attraction was too terrifying. His classmates still suffered nightmares from their previous visit and had chosen another Haunted House in search of something more relaxing.

The proprietor took note of the exchange. He had already recognized Chen Ge. “Your Haunted House can’t be very popular if even your own friends won’t support it. Still, if you insist on learning a few tricks from us, we’re willing to offer the opportunity. No one can accuse us of being ungenerous.”

The man was shrewd. Anyone willing to attack Chen Ge’s business online obviously knew who he was. By admitting him, the proprietor hoped to frighten a rival owner and turn that humiliation into publicity, drawing customers away from Western Jiujiang’s House of Horrors. Chen Ge intended precisely the same thing: each man hoped to win over the other’s audience.

The recent livestream had made Chen Ge’s Haunted House an online sensation, but he knew the attention might last only a week. Tian Teng Medical School attracted less local interest, yet possessed a nationwide reputation and loyal fans such as Su Su.

“Come, help him put on the audio recorder and heart monitor.” The two models walked toward Chen Ge. “Now, we’ll pick the remaining three lucky visitors.”

“That won’t be necessary.” Chen Ge shrugged. “A solo challenge is more entertaining. If you manage to frighten me, I’ll announce on my website that your Haunted House is scarier than mine and promote you for an entire month.”

The man was intrigued by what Chen Ge said, but he was cautious as well. He was sure Chen Ge was up to something. “How are we going to gauge that we’ve managed to scare you?”

“You’ve fitted me with a heart monitor. A normal walking heart rate ranges from sixty to one hundred beats per minute. Fear reduces blood oxygen and makes the heart beat faster.” Chen Ge looked at him calmly. “If my heart rate exceeds one hundred, I lose.”

“Agreed.” The proprietor gave him no chance to reconsider. Even a light jog could push someone’s heart rate over one hundred, never mind genuine fear. As far as he was concerned, Chen Ge had already lost.

“Don’t be so hasty. If I lose, I will admit your Haunted House is scarier than mine online, but what if you lose?”

“If we lose, we’ll likewise announce online that your Haunted House is scarier.” The proprietor gestured toward the crowd. “Everyone here can serve as witness.”

“I do have one small request.” Chen Ge smiled innocently. “I believe your team misunderstands my Haunted House. I hope you’ll visit us in return. I’ve just added a new scenario that hasn’t opened to the public.”

“No problem,” the proprietor promised easily, earning approving cheers. Only He San and Gao Ru Xue looked uneasy. Watching the man, they saw reflections of their former selves.
